items.title: Syria sentences Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia over atrocities
items.description: Bashar al-Assad was sentenced to death after a trial in absentia, convicting him of atrocities committed during Syria's nearly 14-year civil war.

items.title: Ousted Syrian dictator Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia
items.description: The ex-president is convicted of committing war crimes and crimes against humanity during the country's civil war.

items.title: With Middle East still at war, three regional powers ink a new alliance
items.description: The Saudi-Turkish-Pakistani compact is a response to the prolonged Iran war, an Israel perceived as seeking hegemony, and the failure of other diplomatic initiatives. It also anticipates a reduced U.S. regional posture. Does that help the United States?

items.title: Syria court sentences Bashar al-Assad to death for crimes against humanity in absentia
items.description: A Syrian court sentenced ousted Syrian President Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia on Tuesday, along with his younger brother, for crimes against humanity and war crimes during Syria’s 14-year conflict that left about half a million people dead.

items.title: Ukraine’s 40-day campaign has not brought the war closer to an end
items.description: Kyiv is facing a brutal Russian response as its air defence missile stocks dwindle.

items.title: One Killed in Ukrainian Attack on Wildberries Logistics Center in Voronezh
items.description: The online retailer said it evacuated employees from the facility after a fire broke out during the overnight drone strikes.

items.title: Trump pivots back to sanctions for Iran as other strategies to end his war fizzle
items.description: The shift comes as U.S. stockpiles of key weapons have dwindled and as stop-start talks seem again to have stalled. But Trump insists the pressure can lead to a breakthrough.

items.title: Ukraine drone strike on oil refinery deep inside Russia kills at least 13
items.description: Attack hundreds of miles from border would be among deadliest of war as Kyiv aims to strangle Russian economyA Ukrainian drone strike on an industrial city deep inside Russia has killed at least 13 people, according to the local mayor, as Kyiv steps up its campaign of long-range strikes on targets far from the frontlin…

items.title: Russia Reports 13 Dead After Ukrainian Drones Strike In Tatarstan
items.description: Russia said at least 13 people, including a child, were killed in Ukrainian attacks on targets in the central region of Tatarstan, one of Kyiv's deadliest single attacks since the Kremlin launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.

items.title: Is Iran's middle class being pushed into poverty?
items.description: The war has intensified Iran's economic crisis, squeezing household budgets, hurting businesses and raising fears that millions of middle-income families are slipping closer to poverty.

items.title: Sudan: ‘It made me dream again’: The students refusing to let war stop their education
items.description: Sarah Tekhlu was ready to give up on university. An Eritrean refugee, she had already been displaced once from Khartoum to Madani, then again to Port Sudan, as war tore through the country around her. Higher education, she had decided, was a luxury she could no longer afford to want.

items.title: Russian Strike on Zhytomyr Injures 3 Civilians
items.description: A Russian attack on the Zhytomyr region on Aug. 9 injured three civilians and caused fires at civilian infrastructure and private property.
